remediation.issue: Documented commands use aggregate identifiers and artifact paths as shell placeholders without explicit safe quoting.
remediation.suggestion: Require validated identifiers and pass paths as quoted arguments or structured process arguments. Add examples that reject shell metacharacters.

content.value_statement: Project context becomes stale, duplicated, or difficult to retrieve across sessions. This skill organizes authorized notes, preserves source authority, and supports controlled archival and erasure.
actual_capabilities: Initializes private project memory from approved templates after authorization.
Retrieves current context through HOT pointers and dated WARM evidence.
Consolidates duplicate non-canonical notes while preserving conflicts and source authority.
Reviews stale HOT and WARM records for controlled demotion or archival.
Checks broken links, orphaned artifacts, unsupported summaries, and stale references.
Guides authorized subject erasure with minimized logs and explicit scope reporting.
limitations: It cannot change canonical registry facts or accept registry proposals.
It depends on repository-level scripts and references that may be unavailable in standalone installations.
It cannot guarantee deletion from Git history, backups, or external systems.
Persistent writes, promotions, archives, and erasures require explicit authorization.

use_cases.title: Resume Project Work
use_cases.description: Review current priorities, source records, open decisions, and stale context before starting a new session.

use_cases.title: Consolidate Research Notes
use_cases.description: Deduplicate comparable findings, preserve disagreements, repair references, and archive outdated evidence with traceable metadata.

use_cases.title: Handle an Erasure Request
use_cases.description: Plan authorized removal or anonymization, verify consent suppression, and report the limits of working-tree deletion.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the authorized project memory and summarize current priorities. Cite each source path and date. Make no changes.

prompt_templates.title: Initialize Project Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare private memory for this project using the available templates. List proposed paths and request authorization before writing anything.

prompt_templates.title: Consolidate and Archive
prompt_templates.prompt: Find duplicate or stale non-canonical notes in the authorized scope. Preserve conflicts, propose archival actions, and show a dry-run change summary.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Subject Erasure
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an erasure for the confirmed pseudonymous subject identifier. Check affected stores, consent suppression, legal holds, authorization, and deletion limits before execution.

output_examples.input: Review project memory without changing files.
output_examples.output: Current priorities: launch readiness and consent verification. Two WARM sources are older than 90 days. One HOT pointer lacks supporting evidence.

output_examples.input: Consolidate duplicate campaign findings as a dry run.
output_examples.output: Three comparable notes can be merged. One disagreement remains open because observation windows differ. No files were changed.

output_examples.input: Prepare an erasure plan for an approved pseudonymous subject.
output_examples.output: The plan covers working notes, rendered views, projections, exports, indexes, suppression replay, and a minimized operation record. Backups require separate handling.

best_practices: Use read-only review or dry runs before persistent changes.
Keep source dates, registry offsets, authorization references, and exact changed paths.
Store only minimal context and keep personal data, credentials, and production exports outside memory.
anti_patterns: Do not treat cached summaries as canonical truth or current consent.
Do not promote, archive, overwrite, or erase records without explicit authorization.
Do not claim complete erasure when Git history, backups, or external systems remain.

faq.question: What are HOT, WARM, and COLD memory?
faq.answer: HOT stores small current pointers. WARM stores dated working evidence. COLD stores historical notes retrieved only when needed.

faq.question: Can this skill update canonical registry facts?
faq.answer: No. It can prepare authorized proposals, but the owning registry must accept or change canonical facts.

faq.question: Does the skill write files automatically?
faq.answer: No. Persistent writes require explicit authorization unless the current request clearly authorizes the named operation.

faq.question: Can it remove personal data completely?
faq.answer: It can guide working-tree deletion or anonymization. Git history, backups, and external systems need separate approved procedures.

faq.question: Does it work as a standalone skill?
faq.answer: Read-only guidance may work, but initialization and registry workflows depend on repository-level scripts, schemas, and references.

faq.question: How does it handle conflicting notes?
faq.answer: It preserves genuine conflicts, compares authority and scope, and supersedes older notes only when evidence is comparable.
